To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the laser monitoring of the CMS ECAL is reliable and that the response evolution under pion and e-irradiation is adequately followed.
the response loss of the CMS electromagnetic crystals under irradiation can be monitored with a laser light injection system and that the response loss under electron and pions is similar.
the response of PbWO crystals to electrons and pions is well reproduced by the laser monitoring system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the radiation effects in the CMS ECAL.
the development of a laser-based monitoring system to measure the radiation damage in the CMS electromagnetic calorimetry.
the development of the laser monitoring technique to be used in CMS for the ECAL barrel crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monitoring system is able to detect and monitor the response loss of the crystals under pion and electrons irradiation.
the laser monitoring is a reliable tool to monitor the response loss of the ECAL crystals under irradiation.
the monitoring system is a reliable tool to measure the radiation damage in PbWO crystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the monitoring system is a reliable tool for the study of the response loss of the PbWO crystals under different radiation conditions.
the response of the PbWO crystals under irradiation is stable enough to be followed by the monitoring laser system.
the laser monitoring system is a very powerful tool for monitoring the ECAL crystal behavior and for predicting its performance at the LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response loss is well described by the product of two terms: the light collection efficiency and the scintillation yield.
the laser monitoring system is reliable enough to be used for the monitoring of the CMS ECAL crystals.
the response loss of the crystal can be monitored with the laser monitoring system and therefore the crystal aging can be predicted.
